title: My Quarto Website
text:
Hello, I’m Alex, Nice to meet you!



I’m a student in the Masters of Data Science (Computational Linguistics) program at UBC, looking to broaden their horizons with up-to-date trends in AI. I come from a Computer Science background, and am hoping to get the necessary skillset for the Data Science field. I cook, bake, and do gardening in my spare time.

title: More About Me
text: Hello, I’m a student studying currently at the University of British Columbia in the Masters of Data Science (Computational Linguistics). I did my undergrad at University of Victoria, where I used primarily Python, with a Major in Computer Science and a Minor in Linguistics. There, I was first exposed to the basic foundations of AI and Machine Learning, at a time when Natural Language Processing was not yet in full swing as it is now; A result of this was a heavier focus on pre-NLP models and methods (Support vector machines, Bayesian nets, Hidden Markov Models, etc.), and a more casual overview of topics such as tokenization and NLP. Nevertheless, it was there that I developed the interest and curiosity in these topics that led me to take on the MDS-CL program. During this time, I also took on an internship, where I familiarized myself with the industry tools that are used, such as Git and Java servers utilizing the Spring Boot Framework. This gave me an insight on the actual business-related demands of LLMs, not just the theoretical capabilities.

title: More About Me
text:
Future Goals
In the future, I hope to deepen my skills as someone who understands how AI models really work behind-the-scenes, and gain relevant experience from the capstone project for MDS-CL. I’m also looking forward to the career programming aspect that MDS-CL provides training on, as I understand that these aspects are not necessarily intuitive. These skills will help me persist in the Data Science field, which is ultimately the final goal.

title: First weeks of MDS
text:
First Week
On the first day, we got an orientation for then entire MDS program. The room was filled with round tables, and breakfast and lunch were offered. I took this opportunity to connect with some fellow MDS-CL students, as well as the more general MDS-V students. The rest of the orientation was mostly general information distribution for a solid 5 hours, which was a bit hard to sit through, but the entire MDS faculty was introduced, and plagarism and acceptable AI use were explained in great detail. The following day was when the MDS-CL-only cohort had a seperate orientation. We had a campus tour of the buildings in which we’d be having our classes, spanning from the UBC library all the way to the linguistics department offices, which were around a 10-minute walk in between. We also had our first information session by the career programmer, and a past CL student shared their experiences with the crowd.
During the first orientations, it was thoroughly emphasized the sheer volume of work that this program would involve, mainly due to its compact nature: There would be quizzes once every 2 weeks, assignments due every week, and worksheets per lecture for some classes. As I’m settling into the pace of the program, the workload is getting easier to manage. Given, however, that the current material is very introductory and is designed to gradually ease students with not a lot of experience in statistics and programming into the program, the workload at this moment may not be the biggest workload throughout the program.

title: First weeks of MDS
text:
Second week
We’re just barely into the second week, and the workload is already piling up. The main issue is with the volume of work: planning and setting aside time for completion is definitely important for success. A highlight of this week was the clubs day, in which some fellow classmates from the MDS-CL cohort and I participated in by strolling around in one of the main streets at UBC, which was surprisingly tightly packed with booths from various clubs: There were clubs ranging from international student clubs (Ex. Italian, Pakistani, Chinese, etc.) to academic clubs (statistics & data analysis, aerospace engineering, etc.) to hobby clubs (anime, dance, sports, etc.). Unfortunately, the directors of the MDS program did warn that there would not be much leisure time, but checking out the clubs was certaining entertaining in and of itself.
